chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee' from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanee from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a man who has two sister slaves, and he had intercourse with one of them and then had intercourse with the other. He said: 'The first is forbidden to him until the second dies.'

I said: 'What do you think if he sells her?' He said: 'If he sells her merely for his need and no thought of the other enters his mind, then I see no harm in that. But if he sells her so that the first may return to him, then no (it is not permissible).'

From al-Fudayl ibn Ri'ab from al-Halabee from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him, 'A man buys two sisters and has intercourse with one of them and then has intercourse with the other out of ignorance.' He said: 'If he has intercourse with the latter out of ignorance, the first is not forbidden to him. But if he has intercourse with the latter while knowing that she is forbidden to him, both are forbidden to him entirely.'

key_terms.حَرُمَتَا عَلَيْهِ جَمِيعًا: both were forbidden to him entirely

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man having intercourse with two sisters who are slaves, and how does intent affect the prohibition?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the fiqh of *al-Ukhtayn* (two sisters) within the context of slave concubinage, a key area of Shia jurisprudence. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the permanent prohibition caused by intentional intercourse with the second sister and the temporary or non-prohibitive status arising from ignorance (*jahala*) or specific intent during sale, highlighting the nuance between *nikah* and *milk al-yamin*.
